To give a little more context, I'm pretty certain that this has to do directly with two related, but separate, issues.

First of all, North Korea and their flirtations with the nuclear weapon. As-is, it's difficult for Japan to justify an attack against North Korea, even if it looks like a nuclear launch is imminent. The fact that such a strike would be suicidal on North Korea's part is irrelevant to any target, and Japan is likely within striking distance, or will be in the relatively near future, putting them at actual risk. There has been talk of Japan acquiring nuclear weapons because of just this possibility (although that has also met with a lot of protests). Related to this is any potential combat in South Korea and Japan's position on it; given its geographical proximity they would most likely want (or even need) to intervene and may not be able to secure the blessings of the United States in time. Keep in mind that in a situation like this, minutes will literally matter, and taking a half-hour to scramble fighters may make a serious difference in the number of casualties and possibly whether North Korea tries to take out some of Japan on its way down. While the Japanese defense forces may scramble and attack if a strike is indeed imminent, there would be a great deal of trouble after the fact that few will want to deal with, and most of who that do will likely be doing so for political reasons for the most part.

Second, China's movements near Japan. They are essentially trying to colonize the waters between China and Japan, up to and including essentially building artificial islands capable of launching aircraft and manned by the military. They have already begun attempting to assert national jurisdiction around the water and airspace around these islands, which they claim as legitimate Chinese soil. This is more problematic in China insisting their area of sovereignty over the ocean is considerably larger than is the accepted international standard. As there has been very little done about this, and at least a serious potential strategic concern in the future that very directly involves Japan, they are probably readying themselves to react should a conflict break out. While less urgent than a situation in North Korea, they probably want to be prepared. Keep in mind that, should an attack occur, While minutes may not matter, days might, and it will be very hard to make decisions even over the course of days if, say, the country is paralyzed due to an absolutely massive cyber-attack, which some have speculated might be the prelude of a Chinese attack on Japan.

Take this with a grain of salt; again, I'm no professional, but this is the context in which these decisions are being made, as far as I know them. Also, I'm biased, so keep that in mind as well.
